statements.action_statement: No fixed release is available yet; update when Docker Hardened Images publishes one.
statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-18508: when GNU tar extracts with --one-top-level, hardlink targets from the archive are not confined to the top-level directory and resolve relative to the extraction working directory, so a crafted archive can create hardlinks that point outside it and, combined with a symbolic link already present under the working directory, write outside that directory in a single extraction: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-18508, https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2509843. No GNU tar release contains a fix; 1.35 is the latest release. Red Hat fixed it in RHSA-2026:61581 (RHEL 9) and RHSA-2026:61586 (RHEL 10). The only build of this owner published in the DHI Alpine 3.24 repository is 1.35-r5, for x86_64 and aarch64, built from Alpine's tar 1.35-r5 recipe, which builds GNU tar 1.35 with a single patch (ignore-apk-tools-checksums.patch) that does not touch this code: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/a9e2a2dc46f377eb25884f7fea9834492de7f518/main/tar/APKBUILD. Every published build is affected. Until a fix ships, do not rely on --one-top-level as a boundary when extracting untrusted archives; extract them into a new empty directory instead.
